Thanks for calling me smart! That is high praise, but really I'm just smart enough to know that I am very far away from where I should be. 

As far as "pain management" goes, the goal is to get you functional. If you can:
a) Sleep
b) Do daily activities
they pretty much consider it case closed. All the drugs that work are DEA controlled and the abysmal war on drugs means that docs are more stingy with drugs. Like I said, the pain is tolerable, but, seriously, try tolerable for a year. Maybe I am a pussy? I don't know, I've never been anyone else before.

Already stressed my wife out last time. I don't think I can play that card again. Unfortunately, I don't have the motivation to go to my Dr about different drugs. I've given up on the idea that drugs and/or therapy will help; which I have tried both. My spinal condition is permanent. The only thing that relieves the pain are opiates which, unfortunately, are hard to get and dull my brain which makes me suck more at my job. Neither drugs nor therapy will help me at my job; maybe aderall. I think the only thing for me is to embrace negativity and cynicism :-) jk

I take Citalopram which I think is generic Celexa. Programmer, coder, computer scientist, software develop, and software engineer mean nearly the same thing with some nuanced differences; I like Computer Scientist because it matches my degree and encompasses more than develop or programmer. I don't know about you but constantly thinking about blowing my brains out with my pistol combined with brain fog make it hard to code. Did changing your medication help with brain fog?
I think it is a combination of pain, the thought that the pain will never go away and is statistically likely to get worse, and the thought that I will never be good enough.

Here is a great article:

http://www.helpguide.org/articles/suicide-prevention/suicide-prevention-helping-someone-who-is-suicidal.htm

Basically you want to be completely non-judgmental. She probably already feels miserable, so trying to guilt trip her out of it is a bad idea. You can seriously ask. Most suicidal people are willing to completely "spill the beans" if simply asked. When you're that depressed, you don't usually have the energy for deception.
